items.title: Section: Eating, Drinking, Chewing, and Tasting With Clear Awareness

items.zh: 謂噉餅麨、或飯、或糜、或羹、或臛，或有所餘造作轉變可噉可食，能持生命。如是等類皆名為噉。亦名為食。云何為甞？謂甞乳、酪、生酥、熟酥、油、蜜、沙糖、魚、肉、醯、鮓，或新果實，或有種種咀嚼品類。如是一切總名為甞，亦名為食。云何為飲？謂沙糖汁、或石蜜汁、或飯漿飲、或鑽酪飲、或酢為飲、或抨酪飲，乃至於水，總名為飲。
items.en: Chewing means eating flatbread, roasted flour, rice, gruel, soup, or meat broth, or anything else processed and transformed into something chewable and edible, capable of sustaining life — all such things are called chewing, and also called eating. What is tasting? Tasting milk, curd, fresh butter, clarified butter, oil, honey, sugar, fish, meat, vinegar, salted fish, fresh fruit, or various things taken in small bites — all of this together is called tasting. What is drinking? Sugarcane juice, or rock-sugar syrup, or rice-water, or a churned buttermilk drink, or a vinegar drink, or a whey drink, down to plain water — all of this together is called drinking.

items.zh: 若於如是若食、若飲、若噉、若甞所有自相，能正了知；若於一切所食、所飲、所噉、所甞，能正了知；若於爾時應食、應飲、應噉、應甞，能正了知；若於如是應食、應飲、應噉、應甞，能正了知；是名正知。彼由成就此正知故，於自所有若食、若飲、若噉、若甞自知而食，自知而飲，自知而噉，自知而甞；於所應食，於所應飲，於所應噉，於所應甞，正食、正飲、正噉、正甞；應時而食，應時而飲，應時而噉，應時而甞；如所應食乃至如所應甞，如是而食乃至如是而甞。如是名為若食、若飲、若噉、若甞正知而住。若行、若住，廣說乃至若解勞睡正知住者，云何為行？云何為住？云何為坐？云何為臥？云何覺寤？云何為語？云何為默？云何名為解於勞睡？云何於行，廣說乃至於解勞睡正知而住？

items.title: The Four Postures and Wakeful Activity, Briefly Redefined

items.zh: 謂如有一，於經行處來往經行，或復往詣同法者所，或涉道路。如是等類，說名為行。復如有一，住經行處，住諸同法阿遮利耶、鄔波拕耶，及諸尊長、等尊長前。如是等類，說名為住。復如有一，或於大床、或小繩床、或草葉座、或諸敷具、或尼師檀，結加趺坐，端身正願，安住背念。如是等類、說名為坐。復如有一，出住處外洗濯其足，還入住處，或於大床、或小繩床、或草葉座、或阿練若、或在樹下、或空閑室，右脇而臥，重疊其足。如是等類，說名為臥。復如有一，於晝日分經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心；於初夜分、於後夜分經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心；說名覺寤。
items.en: Walking means pacing back and forth in a place set aside for walking meditation, or going to visit a fellow practitioner, or travelling a road. Standing means standing still in a place of walking meditation, or standing before one's teacher of discipline among those of the same Dharma, one's preceptor, venerable elders, or those equal to the venerable. Sitting means sitting cross-legged on a large bed, small rope bed, grass seat, spread mat, or sitting-cloth, holding the body upright, forming a correct resolve, and abiding turned away from unwholesome thought. Lying down means, having washed the feet outside the dwelling and returned inside — whether on a bed, a grass seat, in a forest dwelling, under a tree, or in a quiet room — lying on the right side, one leg resting upon the other. Wakeful activity means practising walking and sitting meditation through the day, and through the first and last watches of the night, purifying the mind of the obstructions.

items.zh: 復如有一，常勤修習如是覺寤，於未受法正受正習，令得究竟。所謂契經、應頌、記別，廣說如前。即於如是已所受法，言善通利，謂大音聲若讀、若誦。或復為他廣說開示。於時時間，與諸有智同梵行者，或餘在家諸賢善者，語言談論，共相慶慰，為欲勸勵及求資具。如是等類，說名為語。
items.en: It is like one who, constantly and diligently practising such wakefulness, properly receives and practices a teaching not yet received, so as to bring it to completion … and, regarding a teaching already received, becomes fluent in its language, reciting or reading it aloud. Or one speaks in order to explain it fully to others. …And from time to time, one converses with wise fellow practitioners, or with virtuous lay people, mutually encouraging one another, so as to exhort and inspire, and also to request the necessities of life. All such things are called speech.

items.title: Two Occasions for Silence: Solitary Reflection and Meditation

items.zh: 復如有一，隨先所聞、隨先所習言善通利究竟諸法，獨處空閑，思惟其義，籌量觀察。或處靜室，令心內住、等住、安住，及與近住、調伏、寂靜、最極寂靜、一趣、等持。或復於彼毘鉢舍那修瑜伽行。如是等類，說名為默。
items.en: It is also like one who, regarding a teaching already fluently mastered through prior hearing and practice, dwells alone in solitude, reflecting on its meaning, weighing and examining it. Or, in a quiet room, one settles the mind inwardly, evenly, and firmly, drawing it near, taming it, calming it, calming it utterly, unifying it, and holding it in balance. Or one cultivates yogic practice through insight meditation. All such things are called silence.

blocks.text: Clear awareness in eating, in the four postures, and in speech and silence. A short untranslated passage (0414c23) concerns eating.

"Eating, drinking, chewing, tasting." Master Cháng Bǎi: chewing is staple food; tasting is side items like milk, curd, butter, honey; drinking is mainly water. Each with clear awareness, in the right measure.

"Standing means standing still in the place of walking meditation, or before one's preceptor or teacher." Master Cháng Bǎi: in walking meditation one does not walk continuously but stops now and then to look inward.
Reciting or reading a teaching aloud ("becoming fluent in its language"); discussing it; teaching it to others. Master Cháng Bǎi: repetition until it is one's own.
Solitary reflection and meditation. Venerable Miào Jìng: after calm, the mind is powerful, and insight can penetrate the true nature of things.
Speech and silence are both part of practice. The treatise does not prize silence for its own sake: one speaks to learn, discuss, and teach, and is silent to reflect and meditate.

quiz.q: How are chewing, tasting, and drinking distinguished, and what is 醯?
options: Cháng Bǎi: chewing is staple food, tasting is side items like dairy and honey, drinking is mainly water; Miào Jìng: 醯 is vinegar
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: chewing is eating staple food; tasting is side items like milk, curd, butter, honey; drinking mainly means water. Venerable Miào Jìng: 醯 is vinegar.

quiz.q: In "standing in a place of walking meditation, before the teachers …," how does Venerable Miào Jìng say 住 should be read?
options: standing — to 住 there is to stand there
quiz.why: "Standing means standing still in a place of walking meditation, or standing before a fellow practitioner's teacher of discipline, one's own preceptor, or other venerable elders." Venerable Miào Jìng: this 住 should be read as "standing" — standing there.

quiz.q: The translator's note says "standing" is distinct from pausing during walking meditation. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: standing is staying put without moving — pausing in the walking area during walking meditation counts too
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: standing is being in one place without moving — for example, in walking meditation one does not walk continuously but stops now and then in the walking area. This contradicts the translator's note.

quiz.q: One occasion for speech concerns a teaching already received. What does one do, and what benefit of repetition does Master Cháng Bǎi note?
options: become fluent and recite it aloud; repeating it many times, one understands it better oneself
give it to others; avoid responsibility
quiz.why: "Regarding a teaching already received, one becomes fluent in its language, reciting or reading it aloud." Master Cháng Bǎi: repeating it many times, the more one speaks the clearer it becomes — this is the second occasion for speech.

quiz.q: Silence includes settling the mind through the nine stages and cultivating insight. How do the masters relate calm, insight, and silence?
options: both say to talk while practising
Miào Jìng: after calm the mind is strong, so insight goes deep; Cháng Bǎi: in insight one does not speak — only the sixth consciousness is at work
both say silence is not reciting
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: after calm the mind is powerful, and insight can penetrate the true nature of things. Master Cháng Bǎi: when practising insight one does not speak; only the sixth consciousness is operating.
